moduleTitle: Using loops for multiple validations in Tricentis Testim
learningObjectives: Articulate how to use loops to test multiple validations in a single test.
Choose the right loop type — Don't repeat, While element, While element text is, For each item, Loop for, or Custom — for a given scenario.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Loops in Testim: six repeat-group types

elements.description: Repeat group configures a group’s repetition; Don’t repeat is the default. Execution conditions and failures can still skip or stop work. The documented maximum is 99 iterations for any loop type, not only fixed-count loops.

elements.title: The six loop types
items: Don’t repeat — no repetition; execution conditions still apply.
While element — repeats depending on whether a target element is Visible (or Not visible).
While element text is — repeats while a target element's text matches an Expected value (supports regex/JS).
For each item — runs the group once per repeating element (e.g. every row in a table), with an item limit (default 99).
Loop for — runs the group a specified number of times, from a literal number or a parameter holding a number (max 99).
Custom — a JavaScript condition with optional parameters and timeout configuration, still subject to the loop limit.

bulletPoints: Loop type is a setting on a group step; Don't repeat is the default (no looping).
While element / While element text is: condition-based, tied to an element's visibility or text.
For each item: one iteration per matching/repeating element (default limit 99).
Loop for: a fixed count — literal number or a numeric parameter (max 99).
Custom: your own JavaScript condition decides whether the loop continues.
The documented 99-iteration maximum applies to every loop type.

elements.description: For each item applies grouped actions to similar matched elements, within the configured item count (maximum 99). Verify actual matched items, iteration results and any paging/virtualization; a loop does not guarantee every record in an arbitrarily large table was visited.
TESTIM_ITERATOR is available within group loops and increments with iterations. It is not a general test-wide parameter outside that scope; use it only where loop parameters are supported.

bulletPoints: 'For each item' = one group of steps, looped once per matching element (e.g. every table row), up to a default limit of 99.
TESTIM_ITERATOR auto-increments each iteration, giving steps inside the loop access to the current index.

elements.term: While element / While element text is
elements.description: While element tests Visible/Not visible; While element text is tests the target’s expected text. Visibility and DOM existence are not interchangeable. Condition timing can be configured; neither loop is unlimited.

Runs the group a fixed number of times — either a literal number typed in directly, or a parameter holding a number, capped at a maximum of 99. Unlike For each item, this doesn't depend on matching elements on the page at all; it's a pure iteration count.

For loop conditions that don't fit any of the built-in types, Custom lets you define the condition as a JavaScript function — with optional JS/HTML parameters passed in, and its own timeout override separate from the test's general settings.

bulletPoints: While element checks visibility; While element text is checks text.
Loop for: a fixed iteration count (number or numeric parameter), max 99 — not tied to page elements.
Custom: your own JavaScript condition, for logic none of the built-in loop types can express.

examPitfalls.title: Hand-writing one validation step per table row
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Manually duplicating a validation step for every row in a data table, breaking whenever the row count changes.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use grouped per-item checks for matched elements, respecting the configured 99 maximum. Verify iteration results and cover paging/virtualized rows separately.

examPitfalls.title: Using 'For each item' when the real need is a fixed repeat count
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Reaching for 'For each item' to repeat a group exactly 5 times, when there's no actual repeating element on the page to iterate over.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use Loop for when the goal is a fixed number of repetitions (literal or parameter-driven) — 'For each item' specifically needs a repeating element to iterate against.

examPitfalls.title: Confusing While element with While element text is
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Picking While element when the actual requirement is about the element's text content, not just whether it's visible.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use While element for a pure visibility condition (Visible/Not visible); use While element text is when the loop should continue based on matching a specific text value in the Expected value field.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What is the primary use case for a 'For each item' loop in Testim?

options.text: Running the entire test suite multiple times.
Running the same set of actions/validations against a list of similar, repeating elements, like table rows.
Retrying a failed step until it passes.
Switching between different browsers during a single run.

practiceQuiz.hint: Think tables with an unknown or variable number of rows.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A 'For each item' loop runs the same actions/validations against similar, repeating elements — such as every row in a table — without hand-duplicating a step per row. It's not about suite-level repetition, retries, or browser switching.

optionExplanations.A: This setting repeats a group, not the entire suite.
optionExplanations.B: It applies the grouped checks to similar matched items within configured limits.
optionExplanations.C: Failure retry is a separate mechanism.
optionExplanations.D: Browser selection is not the purpose of per-item repetition.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What does the TESTIM_ITERATOR parameter provide inside a loop?

options.text: The total number of tests in the project.
The current loop iteration's value, incrementing by one each time the loop runs.
The name of the browser currently running the test.
A random number for test data generation.

practiceQuiz.hint: It's specifically about tracking where you are inside the loop.
practiceQuiz.rationale: TESTIM_ITERATOR is an out-of-the-box parameter that tracks the current loop iteration; its value increases by one each time the loop runs, letting steps inside reference which iteration they're on.

optionExplanations.A: It is not the project’s test count.
optionExplanations.B: It tracks the current iteration within the loop scope.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What must a loop's target be configured as?

options.text: A single, standalone step.
A group step, identifiable by its folder icon, containing the steps to repeat.
An entire separate test.
A Shared Configuration.

practiceQuiz.hint: It has to bundle the steps that will be repeated together.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A loop is configured on a group step — identifiable by the folder icon in its upper-left corner — which contains the steps to include in the loop.

optionExplanations.A: Configure repetition on a group, not an isolated standalone step.
optionExplanations.B: The group contains the steps to repeat.
optionExplanations.C: A separate test is not the Repeat group target.
optionExplanations.D: Configuration selection does not define this repeated group.

practiceQuiz.scenario: For a group with no execution gate preventing it and no failure, what is the default Repeat group choice?

options.text: For each item, with an unlimited item count.
Don’t repeat — the group has no configured repetition.
Custom, requiring a JavaScript condition immediately.
Loop for, defaulting to 99 iterations.

practiceQuiz.hint: The default is explicitly the 'no looping' option.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Don’t repeat is the default repeat setting. This does not override other conditions or failures that can skip/stop execution.

optionExplanations.A: Unlimited repetition is not the default.
optionExplanations.B: Don’t repeat is the default repeat setting.
optionExplanations.C: A Custom condition is not required by default.
optionExplanations.D: The 99 limit does not mean every group defaults to 99 repetitions.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A test needs to repeat a group of steps exactly 5 times, with no element on the page to iterate over. Which loop type fits?

options.text: For each item
While element
Loop for
While element text is

practiceQuiz.hint: It's a fixed count, not tied to elements on the page.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Loop for runs a group a specified number of times (a literal number or a numeric parameter, max 99) — it doesn't depend on repeating page elements, unlike For each item, and it isn't condition-based like the two While loop types.

optionExplanations.A: For each item needs similar matched elements.
optionExplanations.B: A visibility gate does not define the required fixed count.
optionExplanations.C: Loop for implements the stated five repetitions.
optionExplanations.D: A text condition does not define this required fixed count.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What is the difference between While element and While element text is?

options.text: There is no difference — they are the same loop type.
While element checks Visible/Not visible; While element text is checks the target’s expected text.
While element text is can only run once; While element can run indefinitely.
While element requires JavaScript; While element text is never does.

practiceQuiz.hint: Visibility and expected text are distinct checks; neither loop is unlimited.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The first uses a visibility condition and the second uses a text condition. Both remain subject to the documented loop limit and applicable timing configuration.

optionExplanations.A: The loop conditions assert different properties.
optionExplanations.B: One uses visibility; the other uses expected text.
optionExplanations.C: Neither is an unlimited loop; both have documented limits.
optionExplanations.D: The built-in visibility loop does not require custom JavaScript.

quickRecap.value: Default repeat setting; execution gates and failure handling still apply.
Loops based on target element Visible/Not visible.
Loops based on the element's text matching an Expected value.
One iteration per repeating element (default limit 99).
Fixed iteration count — literal or numeric parameter (max 99).
JavaScript condition and timing configuration, subject to the same 99-iteration limit.
Iteration value within group-loop scope, not a general parameter outside loops.
